basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: The atomic balanced posting of one economic event, not the account, the payment or the invoice.
Immutable once posted; corrections are new linked entries.
Separates event time from capture time and preparation from approval and posting.
Unlike a financial statement, it is source-level detail rather than aggregated reporting.

may: Draft a posting and validate balance at the declared scope.
Translate postings to reporting currencies with stated rates.
Screen entries for risk indicators and flag them.
mustNot: Post an entry where debits do not equal credits.
Edit or delete a posted entry.
Approve and post an entry it prepared without a recorded exception.
Backdate an entry without marking capture time.
Erase entries under retention or legal hold.
requiresHuman: Approving manual or unusual journal entries.

considerations: Accurate books protect investors, employees, tax authorities and the public from fraud.
Entries may include personal data of customers and staff.

items: An entry has a ledger identifier, date, lines with accounts, amounts and debit or credit sides, and a source reference.
Often confused with a payment, an invoice, an account balance and a bank statement line.
Misstatement from unbalanced or duplicated postings.
OECD Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T).
